1. Chemical Identity  
 • Name (IUPAC): 4-hydroxybutanoic acid  
 • Common synonyms: GHB; sodium oxybate (when formulated as its sodium salt)

 • Molecular formula/weight: C₄H₈O₃ / 104.10 g·mol⁻¹

3. Mechanism of Action (Pharmacology)  
 • Central agonist at GABA_B receptors; weak agonist at GHB-specific receptors  
 • Enhances inhibitory neurotransmission → sedation, anxiolysis, muscle relaxation  
 • Onset (oral): 15–30 min; duration: 2–4 h  

4. Therapeutic Uses  
 • Sodium oxybate is FDA-approved (Schedule III but with X-DEA restrictions) for:  
    – Narcolepsy-associated cataplexy and excessive daytime sleepiness  
 • Investigational/off-label: alcohol withdrawal syndrome, fibromyalgia (limited data)

 • GHB (unscheduled as pure acid but controlled under “GHB analog” clause, Schedule I)
